mappings.note: MISFILED chemistry (Euro_..._5 Periodic Classification). Identifying the noble gas -- group 18 membership, C 1.1, the only classification competency in this frame.
What isotopes are. Asked here because isotopes are the awkward case for a table ordered by mass, so C 1.1.
Same chemical properties but different atomic masses -- isotopes again, C 1.1. Near-duplicate of qid:104638.
Symbol of manganese -- element symbol recall, which has no home in this frame except C 1.1.
Symbol of potassium -- same as qid:104640, C 1.1.
Number of horizontal rows in the Modern Periodic Table (7 periods) -- table structure, C 1.1.

DEFECT: the stem is degenerate -- the subject has been blanked out, leaving only 'present in modern periodic table', and no model answer is stored. Mapped nonetheless because the stem still names the modern periodic table and C 1.1 is the only competency covering it, so there is no sibling this could wrongly displace. Almost certainly a corrupted twin of qid:104642.
Number of vertical columns known as groups (18) -- table structure, C 1.1.
Degenerate twin of qid:104644 with the count blanked out. Still names 'groups', so C 1.1 for the same reason as qid:104643.
Halogens are group 17 -- group placement, C 1.1.
F and Cl are in group 17 -- the same fact as qid:104646 asked through two members, C 1.1.
Shell count increases down a group -- the period/shell relationship, C 1.1.
Atomic number rises by one across a period -- the ordering principle of the Modern table, C 1.1.
Argon is in period 3 -- configuration to period, C 1.1.
Electrons fill shells in a definite order -- the atomic-structure basis of the table, C 1.1.
Capacity of the K shell is 2 -- shell filling, C 1.1.
Electron capacity follows 2n squared -- the rule behind period lengths, C 1.1.
In 2n squared, n is the shell number. The companion to qid:104653 and the same code.
Definition of atomic radius -- the periodic property itself, C 1.1.
Atomic radius of hydrogen -- the value quoted when radii are compared across period 1, C 1.1.
Atomic radius decreases across a period -- the across-period size trend, C 1.1.
Why radius decreases -- increasing nuclear charge pulling the same shell inward. The cause behind the trend, still C 1.1.
An element showing both metal and non-metal behaviour is a metalloid -- the boundary of the table, C 1.1.
Duplicate of qid:104659 in different words; same code C 1.1 so the pair stays consistent.
Metallic character across a period and down a group -- both directions of the trend in one blank, C 1.1.
Which elements are electronegative (non-metals) -- a periodic trend used to classify, C 1.1.
Which elements are electropositive (metals) -- the complement of qid:104662, same code.
Silicon is a metalloid -- classifying one element by its position, C 1.1.
Calcium is a metal -- same classification task as qid:104664, C 1.1.
Metal oxides are basic. The metal/non-metal classification is C 1.1; the basic character of the oxide is acid-base behaviour, which C 1.3 names explicitly.
Non-metal oxides are acidic -- the mirror of qid:104666 and cited the same way.
Atomic number of beryllium -- the quantity the Modern table orders by, C 1.1.
Atomic mass of hydrogen -- the quantity Mendeleev's table ordered by, C 1.1.
Krypton is a noble gas -- last of the misfiled Euro chemistry run, C 1.1.
The enzyme digesting protein in the small intestine is trypsin -- a step of human nutrition, C 3.2-LO-1.

DEFECT: the stem is truncated mid-phrase ('...occurs during'). Enough survives to fix the subject -- the part where gas exchange happens is the alveolus, which C 4.2-LO-1 names. Mapped on that, but the row needs its ending restored.
Backflow during pumping is prevented by valves -- heart anatomy within the transport pathway, C 3.2-LO-2.
Digestion is completed in the small intestine -- C 3.2-LO-1.
The extracellular fluid leaving the capillaries is lymph -- a component of human transport, C 3.2-LO-2.
Where food is finally digested -- duplicate of qid:104674, same code.

Lime water turns milky with exhaled air because of carbon dioxide. What is tested is that CO2 is a product of respiration, so C 3.2-LO-3 (products and energy) rather than LO-2, which is about the pathway and organs.
Which vertebrates do not pump oxygenated blood from the heart to the body (fishes, single circulation) -- a circulation question anchored on the human double-circulation contrast, C 3.2-LO-2.
The summary equation of photosynthesis -- autotrophic nutrition, C 3.2-LO-1.
The first enzyme to meet food is salivary amylase -- the opening step of human digestion, C 3.2-LO-1.
Cramps from oxygen-starved muscles -- lactic acid from anaerobic respiration, C 3.2-LO-3.
The correct path of urine through the body -- the human excretory pathway and its organs, C 3.2-LO-2.
Which foods are energy foods (carbohydrates) -- food classes within human nutrition, C 3.2-LO-1.
Deriving food from a living host without killing it is parasitic nutrition -- a heterotrophic mode, C 3.2-LO-1.
Fungal nutrition is saprophytic -- C 3.2-LO-1. C 4.1 was considered but the question asks the feeding mode, not the kingdom.

Roots absorb water by osmosis. The named answer is a cell-membrane process, and C 3.1 explicitly covers 'the semi-permeability of cell membrane'. C 4.3-LO-1 is reserved for questions about the xylem pathway rather than the uptake mechanism.
The site of photosynthesis in a leaf cell is the chloroplast -- one of the organelles C 3.1 names. C 3.2-LO-1 would be right for the process; this asks for the organelle.
Amoeba digests food in the food vacuole -- heterotrophic nutrition, C 3.2-LO-1.
What is affected in the mouth without salivary amylase -- starch digestion stalls. C 3.2-LO-1.

Which region absorbs digested food. This names the ORGAN only, so it is a step in the nutrition sequence (C 3.2-LO-1); the structure-function outcome C 4.2-LO-1 is reserved for the versions that ask how the villus achieves it, e.g. qid:85602 and qid:85658.
Contraction and expansion of the food-pipe wall is peristalsis -- C 3.2-LO-1.
Iodine turning rice water blue-black shows starch -- a food test inside the nutrition strand, C 3.2-LO-1. Not C 8.1: no variable is manipulated, the test is simply recalled.
The anal sphincter regulates the exit of unabsorbed food -- the last step of the human nutrition sequence, C 3.2-LO-1.
Vocal cords are in the larynx -- an organ of the human respiratory pathway, C 3.2-LO-2.
Mode of nutrition in fungi -- duplicate of qid:104685 and mapped identically.
Humans have three pairs of salivary glands -- a digestive gland count, C 3.2-LO-1.
